Hi Anita — thanks for the clarity. Attached is a draft activation runway and an evidence pack snapshot for initial review. High level below; detailed week-by-week and gating matrix are in the PDF and the canary sheet.

Key overview (12-week runway):
- Week 0 (contract & infra access): Contract signed, corporate network allowlist in place, KMS exchange initiated, identity provider (IdP) trust configured.
- Weeks 1–2 (sandbox integrations): API keys + webhook endpoints configured; test integrations with non-prod dataset; schema compatibility check (no destructive migrations).
- Weeks 3–4 (staged shadowing): Shadow traffic at 5–10% read-only for validation; KV/prefix caching warmed; telemetry baseline collection.
- Weeks 5–7 (canary): Progressive traffic shift with three gating windows: functional smoke tests, latency P50/P95 thresholds, and error-rate ceilings tied to rollback triggers.
- Weeks 8–10 (broad traffic ramp): Increase to 50% then 100% for non-critical flows; runbook for on-call escalation in place.
- Weeks 11–12 (post-activation validation): SLO burn-in, retention validation, and knowledge-transfer handoff to CedarBank ops.

Integration dependencies (non-exhaustive):
- Network: outbound allowlist for 34.120.0.0/16 and 35.201.0.0/16; TLS mutual-auth option available for private deployments.
- Auth: SAML 2.0/Okta + SCIM for provisioning (we support OIDC as well).
- Data: Schema-read-only shadowing first; mandatory staging snapshot for any write-path activation.
- Observability: Prometheus metrics + OTLP traces; Kibana dashboards (read-only) for CedarBank.

Canary & gating criteria (summary):
- Latency: P50 < 120ms, P95 < 480ms for user-facing routes during canary windows.
- Error rate: application errors < 0.5% and unrecoverable failures < 0.05%.
- Quality checks: automated prompt/regression evals on 500 prompt set; human QA pass-rate > 98% for sampled responses.
- Rollback triggers: sustained breach of thresholds for >10 minutes or single-severity failure affecting >1% sessions.

Contractual dependencies:
- Access: Network IP allowlist, IdP metadata, and a staging DB snapshot (anonymized) by Day 3.
- Downtime: No planned downtime expected; any write-path cutover will be scheduled in a 02:00–05:00 window local to CedarBank time zone.
- Coverage: Redwood will provide 24/7 on-call during the canary weeks; named engineers included in the runbook.

Attachments: Cedar_Activation_Runway_Draft_v1.2.pdf (contains week-by-week Gantt and gating matrix), redwood-evidence-pack-soc2.pdf (SOC2 excerpts), canary-gating-criteria.xlsx (gating spreadsheet).

Next steps: Can we set a 45-minute technical handoff tomorrow at 10:00 PT to walk the Gantt and gating sheet? If that works I will send a calendar invite and a focused agenda.

Best,

Anita / team — adding the engineering-level runbook details you asked for; pulled key excerpts here to keep the inbox-light. The attached canary sheet has the gating thresholds and an example of a three-stage canary timeline.

Technical integration steps (ordered):
1) Staging credentials & whitelist -> Redwood provisioned sandbox project; verify network egress and DNS.
2) IdP SAML test flow -> confirm group membership mapping for admin/test roles.
3) Schema validation -> run our dry-run tool against your anonymized snapshot; flags must be zero for write-path activation.
4) Telemetry hook -> OTLP endpoint and sampling config (we recommend 25% sampling for traces during canary).
5) Shadow traffic -> run 72-hour shadow at 5–10% to collect baseline, validate caching behavior and KV warmup.
6) Canary run -> three waves (2%, 10%, 33%) each with a 4-hour observation window and automated rollback checks.

Canary gating automations we will enable:
- Automatic rollback on error-rate spike > 0.5% for 10m with escalation page to Redwood on-call.
- Latency guardrail: if P95 exceeds configured threshold by >20% for two consecutive windows we pause ramp.
- Regression eval: nightly batch of 1,000 prompts compared to staged golden prompts; any drop >0.8% in quality metric pauses rollout.

DB/write cutover approach:
- Principle: avoid in-place destructive migrations. We will perform a blue-green pattern when write-path is required: shadow -> feature flag gating -> controlled cutover with dual-write if customer-side accepts. Full rollback path included.

On-call & escalation:
- Redwood will list two primary engineers for the canary week and provide pager + Slack bridge. We will also join CedarBank on-call for the primary ramp windows.

References in attachments: canary-gating-criteria.xlsx (detailed thresholds and alerts), runbook-excerpt.txt (sample escalation flow), Cedar_Activation_Runway_Draft_v1.2.pdf (Gantt).

Let us know any additional security artifacts required (we can pull deeper SOC2 controls or FedRAMP-first pass if needed, timeline for extra evidence is ~7 business days).

Thanks — Priyom

Hi Olga / Priyom — appreciate the fast turnaround and the level of detail. Procurement asked me to confirm a couple of contractual items before we issue the PO: 

- DocuSign: please provide the final SOW/Service Addendum with the 12-week activation runway called out and the names of the on-call engineers so we can attach to the PO.
- SSO: CedarBank requires SAML metadata and a test IdP integration checklist; can you confirm you support the latest Okta metadata URL pattern and share the example metadata?
- Evidence: the SOC2 excerpt is fine for initial sign-off; Procurement may request a full controls report during legal review.

If you can push the signed SOW and the SAML metadata by EOD Monday we will route the PO and lock a target start date the following week. Also: please include an itemized list of any downtime windows or actions that could impact customer-facing services.

I'll book the intake slot for next Tue at 10:00 PT for the technical run-through; expect an invite.

Thanks — Vikram
